question: Does a fast, typed second judge (JEV's role) separate true from false status-setting findings better than the verifier's own confidence?
standIn: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (JEV is waitlist only; no TypeSafe key). Developer measurement on Felipe's Anthropic key (2026-10-15: 'If the Anthropic key works for that, sure, run it'); never product code. Temperature 0, typed JSON {p_accurate, p_real}, system asks for calibrated probabilities.
input: Each labeled finding's statement and its cited file (up to 24,000 characters), the same file the labelers start from; not the rest of the repository.
population: Every labeled finding of release attempts 3, 4 and 5 (docs/evaluation/runs): 371 judged, 334 strictly true, 37 false.
conclusion: Worse than chance (AUC below 0.5): the false findings left are judgment errors that need the whole repository (a README declaring a demo, middleware, whether an id is ever exposed), and a fast judge given only the cited file cannot see them. A calibrated judge helps only if it reads the evidence the labelers read; JEV's value is not established and nothing is gated on this stand-in.
